approach: No author implementation is available, so rebuild the Table 1 computation in Python from the paper. Download the WWGbook autism data, apply the known age weights by multiplying Y, X and Z by 1/age, and fit the child-level random-intercept/random-age-slope LMM by REML with expected information. For each covariance parameter, profile the remaining parameters over the extended positive-definite marginal-covariance set, evaluate the modified profile-score statistic, and invert it by outward secant search. Compute all four intervals to cross-check C1-C4 but write the C1 psi2 endpoints as the primary metric; validate against the reported REML point estimates and the reported endpoints before the final run.

files.purpose: Central paths, model specification, optimizer/root-search tolerances, and Table 1 validation values.
Download/extract the WWGbook CRAN package, load the autism data, validate 610 rows/158 children, build age weights and the transformed Y, X and Z matrices.

Build the full marginal covariance, check positive definiteness, evaluate REML log-likelihood, score and expected information; fit the REML estimate using a trust-region optimizer with expected information as the Hessian proxy.
For a fixed covariance parameter, maximize REML over the remaining parameters on the extended positive-definite set and compute the modified profile-score statistic T.
Invert T for each psi parameter by warm-started outward secant/regula-falsi search, handling covariance versus variance ranges and recording runtimes.
Tiny data-flow test on a subset of children: load data, fit REML, evaluate one profile statistic, and assert finite output and positive-definite covariance.
Single entrypoint: load data, fit REML, compute all four intervals, validate C1, and write results/metrics.json.

config.paper: arXiv 2610.04181 (paper_only route; authors repository koekvall/reconf-suppl is unavailable)
config.target_claim: C1: psi2 95% profile-score interval lower endpoint (-34.566, -18.401)

data.age_centering: raw age in years, origin age=0 (A1, high risk)
data.missing_data: use all observed rows, no imputation (A6)
data.group_coding: treatment coding, first sorted group level as baseline (A2)

model.fixed_effects: Eq (13) as printed: intercept + age + age^2 + G dummies + age:G + age^2:G; if Eq (13) is unavailable, use the WWGbook autism convention vsae ~ age + age^2 + sicdegp + age:sicdegp + age^2:sicdegp with random (age|childid)
model.random_effects: child-specific random intercept and random slope in age; Psi = [[psi1, psi2], [psi2, psi3]] (R8)
model.error: psi4 I on the transformed scale; original error variance proportional to age^2 (R1, R9)
model.weights: w_it = age_it^-2; multiply Y, X and Z by sqrt(w_it)=1/age_it (R9, A7)
model.covariance_derivatives: A1 = blockdiag(ones), A2 = blockdiag(ab'+ba') with a=1/age and b=1, A3 = blockdiag(ones), A4 = identity on the transformed scale (R1, R9)

reml_fit.optimizer: custom trust-region with expected information as Hessian proxy; fallback to scipy L-BFGS-B with multi-start if trust-region fails (R11, A4)
reml_fit.multi_start: diagonal/moment starts plus small negative covariance starts; do not start from reported Table 1 endpoints (A8)
reml_fit.pd_check: Cholesky of the full marginal covariance Sigma(psi) must succeed (A9)

profile.nuisance_set: extended set: maximize over all remaining psi with Sigma_i(psi) positive definite for every child; do not impose PSD on Psi itself (R5, A9)
profile.nuisance_method: exact restricted-likelihood profiling over the extended slice; one-step approximation only as documented fallback (R6, A3)
profile.warm_start: true; use previous slice optimum as start for next candidate (R12)

test_statistic.score: S_a = -0.5 tr(P A_a) + 0.5 r' Sigma^{-1} A_a Sigma^{-1} r with P = Sigma^{-1} - Sigma^{-1}X(X'Sigma^{-1}X)^{-1}X'Sigma^{-1} (R3, R4)
test_statistic.expected_information: I_ab = 0.5 tr(P A_a P A_b); do not use observed information (R3, R4)
test_statistic.T: T_j(c) = S_j(c, eta_hat)^2 * (I(c, eta_hat)^{-1})_{jj}, where I is the expected REML information matrix at the profile nuisance optimum (R3, R4)

interval_search.method: outward search from REML estimate; warm-started secant/regula falsi with bisection safeguard (R12, A5)

validation.point_estimate_tolerance: abs error <= 0.05 for each REML estimate; if larger, diagnose fixed-effect specification, age origin, group coding and weights before proceeding
validation.endpoint_tolerance_C1: 10% relative error on each endpoint's absolute magnitude (contract tolerance)

runtime.reported_reconf_seconds: 0.5 s for four intervals (paper C5; not the target)
runtime.measure: record wall time for the four profile-score intervals only

steps: Create directories results/ and src/. Install dependencies with `python -m pip install --quiet pyreadr rdata requests numpy scipy`.

Implement src/config.py with the constants above, then implement src/data.py. Download the WWGbook source tarball using requests, extract with tarfile, locate the autism .rda/.RData file, and load it with pyreadr (fallback to rdata). Convert to a pandas DataFrame, validate 610 rows and 158 unique child IDs, and cache data/autism.csv.

Build the transformed design in src/data.py: sort by childid and age; create the Eq (13) fixed-effect matrix X (intercept, age, age^2, treatment-coded group dummies, age-by-group, age^2-by-group); set Z=[1, age] per child; multiply Y, every X column and both Z columns by sqrt(w)=1/age.

Implement src/lmm.py: assemble the 610x610 block-diagonal Sigma(psi)=Z Psi Z' + psi4 I from the transformed rows; implement a positive-definite check by Cholesky; implement REML log-likelihood, analytic score S, and expected information I_ab=0.5 tr(P A_a P A_b) using full 610x610 matrices.

Implement the REML fit in src/lmm.py using a custom trust-region optimizer with gradient=-S, Hessian=I and backtracking on objective increase or non-positive-definite Sigma. Use diagonal/moment multi-starts and fallback L-BFGS-B. Verify the fitted point estimates match Table 1 (46.089, -24.727, 13.993, 2.521) within 0.05; if not, diagnose age origin and fixed-effect design against Eq (13) before continuing.

Implement src/profile.py: for target parameter j and candidate c, fix psi_j=c, maximize REML over the other three parameters on the extended set where full Sigma is positive definite. Use warm starts, the same expected-information trust-region, and return eta_hat, S_j, I, and T_j(c)=S_j^2*(I^{-1})_{jj}.

Write validation checks: T at the REML estimate should be near zero; T at the reported psi2 endpoints -34.566 and -18.401 should be close to 3.84146. If the endpoints give T far from 3.84, check the weight transform, expected-information formula, extended-set handling and fixed effects.

Implement src/intervals.py: for each psi parameter, start at the REML estimate, step outward in the allowed range, bracket the first point where T>3.84146, then refine with warm-started secant/regula falsi and bisection safeguards until |T-q|<1e-6 or |c-c'|<1e-6. Record each interval and wall time.

Write smoke_test.py: load the full data, select about 30 children including every group level, fit REML on this subset, evaluate one T at psi2_hat-1, and assert finite T, positive-definite covariance and score norm below tolerance.

Write reproduce.py: run the full pipeline, compute all four intervals, write results/metrics.json with the psi2 interval, both endpoints, absolute/relative errors versus (-34.566,-18.401), the other three intervals, REML point estimates, T values at endpoints, runtimes, and pass/fail flags. Run `python reproduce.py` twice and confirm identical numbers within numerical tolerance.
smoke_test: Run `python smoke_test.py`. It loads the WWGbook autism data, subsets to about 30 children including all expressive-language groups, builds the transformed Y/X/Z, fits the REML model, evaluates one profile statistic T(psi2_hat-1) with nuisance profiling, and asserts finite T, Cholesky success, and score norm <1e-5.
intermediate_checks: Data check: exactly 610 observed rows, 158 unique child IDs, ages subset {2,3,5,9,13}, outcome vsae and group sicdegp present; report missingness before filtering.
Design check: transformed X has full column rank; each child has two random-effect columns [1/age, 1] after weighting; no zero or non-finite ages.

Model-spec check: REML point estimates match Table 1: psi1=46.089, psi2=-24.727, psi3=13.993, psi4=2.521 within 0.05 absolute. If not, test raw versus centered age and the Eq (13) fixed-effect terms; do not tune to endpoints.
Derivative check: analytic REML score matches finite differences of the REML log-likelihood at random interior psi values with relative error <1e-4.
Information check: expected information matrix is symmetric and positive definite; verify T at the REML estimate is <0.05.
Strong validation check: evaluate T at the reported psi2 endpoints -34.566 and -18.401; both should be within a few percent of 3.84146. Also check the reported psi1, psi3 and psi4 endpoints.

Extended-set check: at each nuisance optimum, full Sigma is positive definite (Cholesky succeeds) and the free-parameter score norm is <1e-5; verify Psi itself is allowed to be indefinite when Sigma is positive definite.
Smoke test must pass before the full run; abort if any Cholesky, optimizer, or profile evaluation fails.
budget_plan: Total reference budget 30 min: 5 min environment and CRAN/data download, 3 min smoke test, 10 min full REML fit plus four interval searches (each interval is only a few seconds), 2 min metrics and repeat run, with 10 min reserved for diagnosing any Table 1 point-estimate mismatch. The numerical work itself is seconds; most budget is setup and validation.
